name: Helan Mountain East
description: China's most credible fine-wine region, on the desert flank of the Helan mountains, where vines are buried under earth every winter to survive the cold.
funFact: Ningxia growers bury their vines under soil each autumn and unearth them each spring, because winter temperatures would otherwise kill them — an enormous annual labour cost that no other serious wine region carries.

serve.how: Decant young bottles for around an hour. Serve cool in a large glass. Ningxia Cabernet tends toward firm tannin and pronounced oak in its ambitious bottlings, so give it air. The region is young enough that vintage-to-vintage variation is still wide; recent vintages are markedly better than early ones.

composition.summary: Desert-grown Bordeaux varieties on gravelly alluvial soils under irrigation.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Cabernet Gernischt.

components.label: Region
components.detail: The eastern foothills of the Helan Mountains in Ningxia, on the edge of the Gobi.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Destemmed, fermented warm with extended maceration.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: 12–24 months in French and American oak, often substantially new.

composition.process: An arid, high-altitude desert climate with irrigation gives precise ripening control, though vines must be buried each winter to survive temperatures that would otherwise kill them.

name: Nashik
description: India's wine capital, on a plateau above Mumbai, where the vines are pruned twice a year and the harvest happens in February.
funFact: In India's tropical climate vines never go dormant, so growers prune twice annually — once to grow foliage and once to set fruit — and harvest in late winter rather than autumn.

serve.how: Serve well chilled in a standard white glass. Nashik whites are made for freshness and for Indian food, so drink them young and cold. Sauvignon Blanc and Chenin are the strengths; the sparkling wines from the same region are also worth attention and should be served colder still.

composition.summary: Tropical-plateau whites harvested in winter under a double-pruning regime.

components.label: Grapes
components.detail: Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc and Viognier.

components.label: Region
components.detail: The Nashik plateau in Maharashtra, at 600–900 metres above sea level.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Cool stainless fermentation under temperature control.

composition.process: Altitude tempers a tropical climate, and a double-pruning cycle produces a February harvest, with cold stainless fermentation preserving the aromatics for early drinking.

name: Yamanashi
description: Koshu — a pink-skinned grape grown in Japan for over a thousand years — made into a delicate, low-alcohol white built expressly to sit beside raw fish.
funFact: Koshu carries genes from wild Chinese vine species and reached Japan along the Silk Road; DNA work confirmed it is a genuine Vitis vinifera hybrid rather than a European import.

serve.how: Serve well chilled in a standard white glass. Koshu is deliberately delicate — low in alcohol, subtle in aroma, with a faint phenolic grip from its pink skins — so it is easily overwhelmed. Pair it with sashimi or lightly dressed fish rather than anything rich, which is exactly what it was revived to do.

composition.summary: A delicate, low-alcohol white from the indigenous pink-skinned Koshu grape.

components.label: Region
components.detail: The Kofu basin in Yamanashi prefecture, ringed by mountains west of Tokyo.

components.label: Vinification
components.detail: Gentle pressing with cool stainless fermentation; some sur lie versions.

components.label: Aging
components.detail: Usually unoaked; occasional lees ageing for texture.

composition.process: A humid climate and a thick-skinned pink grape give low sugar and subtle aromatics, handled gently and fermented cold to preserve the wine's deliberate delicacy.
